extracted.intended_audience: makers, startup founders, product writers, and bloggers who want to get traffic from Hacker News
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for submitting Show HN posts and blog/product links to Hacker News to maximize votes, engagement, and homepage visibility. Covers what topics work, how to title and describe posts, timing, vote-getting tactics, commenting etiquette, and follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic suitability — what works on Hacker News
rubrics_metrics.description: Topics that tend to perform well include tech history, hot takes (slightly contrarian views), data-driven posts, bugs/issues discovered while building, geeky projects (e.g., eInk, Raspberry Pi), and drama about tech/social-media/product design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given: command palettes, Markdown history, Canon Cat, TED talk time limit, notes apps critique, enterprise software views, research like YC companies not using .com, why software prices are rising. The more obscure/hidden and passionately presented the topic, the better.

rubrics_metrics.name: Passion and depth
rubrics_metrics.description: HN responds to passion — dig deep, build something you love, and share how you built it and what you learned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice: fall down a rabbit hole, nerd out on something you love, share contrarian opinions you’d enjoy debating. Passion generates comments and engagement even if polarizing (e.g., Dropbox example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Show HN for playable products
rubrics_metrics.description: Show HN is for something you've made that other people can play with; use it to share product launches that are ready for users to sign up and try—nothing else.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show HN gives a slightly better than 1/10 chance to get an audience. Major new versions with deep changes may be reshared, but usually one Show HN is your launch shot. Show HN posts also appear on the Show HN page even if they fall off /newest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show HN title format
rubrics_metrics.description: Start Show HN titles with the exact text 'Show HN: ' followed by your product name, then typically a comma or dash, followed by a tagline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taglines should state the use-case (e.g., 'minimalist scoring tool for board games'), be in active voice, avoid passive phrasing like 'app that offers', and be 50 or fewer characters. Use the same post title both on your blog and when sharing on HN.

rubrics_metrics.name: General post title rules — don’t editorialize
rubrics_metrics.description: For most posts, share the exact title of the post along with its URL. Don’t editorialize, and absolutely never put a title that the URL doesn’t deliver on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write the post title with an eye to what will catch HN’s interest, but ensure the URL content matches the title to avoid downvotes. Use that carefully-crafted title both on your site and on HN.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show HN description guidance and length
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a 1–200 word description in the Show HN text box describing the product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best descriptions tend to sound friendly, casual, and personal; be written in first person ('I’ve been working on'); explain why you built it and why others will want it; be geeky (brief stack/how built); include caveats if beta; end with a 'thanks'. You may include secondary links (founding story, details) in the description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title voice and phrasing — use active voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Use active voice in titles and avoid phrases like 'app that offers' or other passive constructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active, specific phrasing that states the use-case tends to perform better (especially in Show HN taglines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Best time to post
rubrics_metrics.description: Mid-week is generally the best time to post; people are busiest Monday and share on Friday, so mid-week gets more attention. Weekends have less competition but more casual readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author posts early-morning Europe time to capture Asian afternoon/European morning momentum feeding into East Coast. Key goal: maximize time on front page. Practical heuristic: check news.ycombinator.com/newest; if the last post on the page was posted an hour or more ago, it’s relatively quiet and your post may have a better chance to stay on /newest longer and gain votes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show HN page visibility advantage
rubrics_metrics.description: Show HN posts appear on the Show HN page even if they fall off the /newest page, giving them an extra chance for comments, votes, and traffic (or to hit the front page later).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This can be especially valuable if a post doesn’t immediately land on the homepage.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to get votes organically
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary route: post on HN and wait for organic votes; supplement by sharing elsewhere without directly asking for upvotes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch /newest to ensure your post is live and give it time. Tweet or share elsewhere but avoid telling people to upvote on HN; instead, hope followers who use HN submit it themselves. Asking people to go to /newest and find your post to upvote is an acceptable tactic (don’t share a direct link to the post requesting votes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tactical solicitation (do it carefully)
rubrics_metrics.description: You can message a dozen+ people asking them to find your post on /newest and upvote, but don’t ask the same people every time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Better to ask different people across submissions or build a following so your name alone draws votes. Avoid posting a direct link and telling people to upvote since direct votes don’t count and look like solicitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting ring caution
rubrics_metrics.description: Hacker News monitors for voting rings; if the same people always upvote your content right after it’s published, votes may be removed and/or your post hidden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid coordinated, repeated immediate upvotes from the same small group. Rotate people you ask and aim for organic distribution of early votes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Votes needed and momentum matters
rubrics_metrics.description: It can take as few as a handful of votes to be visible; typically at least a dozen or so are needed to hit the homepage, and the quicker the votes come in, the faster you’ll hit the homepage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: a post with 4 votes could be position 30 on homepage; posts getting a dozen votes quickly can reach the top. Momentum and timing of votes influence ranking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don’t solicit more upvotes once on homepage
rubrics_metrics.description: Once your post is on the Hacker News homepage, don’t try to solicit more upvotes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let votes come organically after reaching the homepage; active solicitation at that point is discouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmitting strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: If a post doesn’t catch fire, you can resubmit it after a delay, but not too soon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Show HN, typically only post at launch or for major new releases. For blog posts, try re-submitting a couple weeks later at a different time — sometimes a post does poorly once and succeeds later, or can get a second life much later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commenting etiquette for authors
rubrics_metrics.description: If someone else shares your article, it's good to jump in and comment that you’re the author/founder and that you’re excited; reply to comments and engage with feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Show HN, the founding team’s commentary shows at the top so don't add other top-level comments. Reply to all comments as much as possible, even negative ones, and try to diffuse negativity politely. Include links in replies only when directly asked or clearly relevant—otherwise links look self-promotional and risk downvotes/flags. Have thick skin and be constructive.

rubrics_metrics.name: General commenting contribution standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Before posting a comment, ask 'Does your comment teach us anything?'. If not, maybe don’t post.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Join other conversations constructively so you’re not only ever promoting your own work. Value-add comments that teach or inform are encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-homepage follow-up and conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximize the value of HN traffic by having a newsletter signup and by monitoring social shares and backlinks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check Twitter/X and other networks for people sharing your post; like/reply to those posts. Use Google Analytics and Ahrefs to find links and potential partners, and plan follow-up outreach or content to convert interested visitors into subscribers or partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realistic expectations and persistence
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat HN as an occasional growth channel — a ~1 in 10 hit rate is a reasonable metric; keep shipping and publishing rather than relying on any single post.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don’t take it too seriously when posts don’t gain traction. Keep trying, iterate on posts and submissions, and aim for consistent output so one of your items eventually lands.
